capitals.note: 1086-1092 as a Castilian vassal under al-Qadir; 1094-1099 under the Cid; 1099-1102 under Jimena.

rulers.name: Abd al-Aziz al-Mansur
rulers.note: Grandson of Almanzor; 'ruled for about 40 years until his death in 1061'. The list also has Mujahid al-Amiri (in Dénia) 1017-1021, with a citation needed.

rulers.note: Annexed to Toledo in 1065 (Al-Ma'mun of Toledo 1065-1075 and Yahya al-Qadir 1075-1085 ruled Valencia from Toledo).

rulers.title: Castilian vassal

rulers.name: Jimena Díaz
rulers.title: regent

rulers.name: Ibn 'Iyad
rulers.note: 1145-1146 and 1146-1147 on the list; Sayf al-Dawla (Zafadola) commanded January-February 1146.

correction.text: unchanged for 1010-1037; the larger shape of 1040 applies from 1038

keyframe_review.note: 11,897 km2 (49 grid cells: Valencia and its district) against an infobox that states no area. Drawn 1010-1037 only: from 1038 the Valencia of the pages also holds Almería and Murcia (the 1040 shape). Mujahid of Dénia is listed as ruler of Valencia 1017-1021 (citation needed); no page opened gives the land he held, so the shape stands.

correction.text: unchanged shape, drawn 1038-1040: Valencia, Almería and Murcia

keyframe_review.note: 32,845 km2: Valencia plus Almería plus Murcia. The Almería page has 'From 1038 to 1041 Almería belonged to the Taifa of Valencia' (infobox 'To Valencia: 1038-1042'); the Murcia page has 'To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065'. So draw this shape 1038-1040 instead of 1040-1045 (Almería leaves in 1041; Murcia stays; see the new keyframe taifa-of-valencia_1041). Shape not compared with an infobox area: none is stated.

correction.text: Valencia and Murcia, Almería independent again from 1041

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1041-1045: Valencia and Murcia without Almería, which the Valencian governor Ma'n 'declared independent again' (list entry 1041; infobox 'To Valencia: 1038-1042'). The shape is Cliopatria's own 1046 shape, drawn five years earlier.
18,195 km2: Valencia and the Murcian lands, which the Murcia page gives to Valencia 1038-1065 ('To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065'); Murcia is independent again 1065-1078.

11,922 km2 (the 1010 core less one cell) for 1085-1093. Alfonso VI took Toledo in 1085; 'Alfonso installed al-Qadir in Valencia as his vassal' (1086, 'Castilian vassal state under al-Qadir, garrisoned by Castilians' 1086-1092); Ibn Jahhaf's coup was October 1092. The vassal tint belongs to the Castile dossier (vassal_start with counterpart taifa-of-valencia), which has no such event.
11,848 km2 for 1094-1098: the Cid entered Valencia on 15 June 1094 and 'ruled directly as king', building fortresses south of the city near Xàtiva and capturing Almenara in 1097.

correction.text: Valencia under Jimena Díaz until the evacuation of April-May 1102

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1099-1102: Cliopatria has no Valencia shape between 1099 and 1146. The Cid died 10 July 1099 and 'his wife Jimena took charge'; the Almoravid Mazdali besieged the city in early spring 1102 and the Almoravids occupied it in April-May 1102. The 1094 shape is reused.

correction.text: Valencia city and district under Qadi Marwan and Ibn 'Iyad

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1145-1147: the Almoravid collapse; 'March 1145: Qadi Marwan was pressured into leading the city as ra'is', then Ibn 'Iyad; 'independent from the Almoravids 1145'. The page names the city only; the 1094 shape is reused. The Murcia page's infobox has 'To Valencia: 1145-1147' for Murcia (a personal union under Ibn 'Iyad); the Murcia dossier draws Murcia on its own.

correction.text: Valencia and its district until August 1147; then part of Ibn Mardanish's realm ruled from Murcia

keyframe_review.note: 53,704 km2 for 1147-1151 reaches Teruel, Albacete, Tarragona and Lleida (41.8 N); no page opened supports it. Ibn Mardanish 'established rule over Murcia, Valencia, and Dénia' and based himself in Murcia with his brother Yusuf governing Valencia (Valencia page), so from August 1147 Valencia lies in the Murcian realm (the Murcia dossier carries the gain). Use the Valencia city shape for January-August 1147 and nothing in this dossier afterwards.

correction.text: Valencia and nearby areas, including Puig, under Zayyan ibn Mardanish

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1228-1235: Cliopatria has no Valencia shape between 1173 and 1235. 'Late 1228 or early 1229: Abu Zayd was overthrown, the Almohads left, and Zayyan ibn Mardanish took control'; territory 'Valencia and nearby areas, including Puig'. The 1236 shape is reused.

7,761 km2: 'In 1236 Aragon occupied nearby Puig, and Zayyan was defeated at the Battle of the Puig'; the final siege began 23 April 1238 and 'the city surrendered' on 29 September 1238. The shape is drawn only to September 1238, not to 1240. The Kingdom of Valencia page: conquest 'started in 1232', Borriana and Peñíscola 1233 (north of this shape), James I entered the city 9 October 1238.

correction.text: unchanged cells but not this state's: the unconquered south of the Valencian lands until 1243-1245

keyframe_review.note: 6,255 km2 for 1241-1249 is not the Taifa of Valencia, which ended in September 1238 ('dawn of the Kingdom of Valencia', 9 October 1238). If the cells (24 of 26 lie in Valencia province) are still Muslim-held, no page opened names the ruler; the Kingdom of Valencia page has 'A third phase started in 1243 and ended in 1245' and 'The Treaty of Almizra established the south line of Aragonese expansion' (the Crown of Aragon dossier dates it 26 March 1244). Drawn for no state here; assign to the Crown of Aragon dossier or a gap-filler.

ledger.note: 1010: Mubarak and Muzaffar make Valencia independent. '1010-1011: Former slaves Mubarak and Muzaffar established Valencia's effective independence, having previously been irrigation officials there' (infobox 'Established c. 1010'); the page names the city and its surroundings, not a boundary.

1038: Valencia takes Almería. 'From 1038 to 1041 Almería belonged to the Taifa of Valencia' after Zuhayr's death left a power vacuum and the emir Abd al-Aziz occupied it (infobox 'To Valencia: 1038-1042'). Cliopatria draws the larger Valencia shape from 1040.

region.text: the Murcian lands, held by Valencia 1038-1065

ledger.note: 1038: Valencia holds Murcia. The Murcia page infobox 'To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065'. Cliopatria's Valencia shape includes the Murcian lands from 1040.

1041: Almería is independent again. The Valencian governor Ma'n 'declared Almería independent again' (list entry 1041; the text 'From 1038 to 1041'); the infobox has 1038-1042, so 1041 is the text's year.
1065: Murcia becomes independent again. The page lists Murcian independence 'from 1065 to 1078', the end of the Valencian period (infobox 1038-1065).

region.text: Valencia and its district, 'absorbed into the Taifa of Toledo' 1065-1085

ledger.note: 1065: Toledo annexes Valencia. 'Al-Ma'mun of Toledo seized Valencia, annexing it to the Taifa of Toledo, and installed his vizier as governor' (key dates 'annexed by Toledo 1065'); Ferdinand I had attacked the city shortly after Abd al-Malik's accession.

1085: Valencia is its own again. No page dates when Valencia left Toledo's control (it 'began slipping' after 1075; Alfonso VI took Toledo in 1085); Alfonso 'installed al-Qadir in Valencia as his vassal' and 'Valencia accepted the rule of Al-Qádir' in early March 1086. Cliopatria's Valencia shape resumes in 1085. Bridging judgment.

October 1092: Qadi Ibn Jahhaf overthrows al-Qadir. 'Qadi Ibn Jahhaf led a coup while El Cid was away. Al-Qadir was captured and executed after Almoravid warriors arrived.' Same state, new ruler (the Castilian vassal ends; the Castile dossier should close its vassal event).

15 June 1094: El Cid takes Valencia. 'El Cid re-entered Valencia after a 20-month siege and ruled directly as king'; the Almoravids besieged it in October 1094 and were defeated. The page's infobox gives 'conquered by El Cid 1094'.

region.text: Almenara, taken after a three-month siege

ledger.counterpart: Almenara's Muslim holders (the page names none)
ledger.note: 1097: the Cid captures Almenara. 'El Cid captured Almenara after a three-month siege'; the page names no holder, and the same year the Almoravids routed the Castilians at Consuegra.

1102: the Almoravids occupy Valencia. After the Cid's death on 10 July 1099 'his wife Jimena took charge'; Mazdali besieged the city in early spring 1102 and, after the April-May evacuation with Alfonso VI's help, 'The Almoravids then occupied the city'.

March 1145: Valencia is independent of the Almoravids. 'Almoravid authority collapsed, and local communities formed new taifas'; 'Qadi Marwan was pressured into leading the city as ra'is' in March 1145, then Ibn 'Iyad deposed him (key dates 'independent from the Almoravids 1145').

region.text: Valencia city under Ibn Mardanish's governor Yusuf

ledger.note: August 1147: Valencia passes to Ibn Mardanish. 'Ibn 'Iyad died and passed command to Ibn Mardanish, who ruled eastern al-Andalus from Murcia, with his brother Yusuf governing Valencia'; he 'established rule over the cities of Murcia, Valencia, and Dénia' (Ibn Mardanish page). The state lies dormant until 1228; the Almohads annex the realm in 1172 (Murcia dossier).

Late 1228: Zayyan ibn Mardanish takes Valencia. 'Late 1228 or early 1229: Abu Zayd was overthrown, the Almohads left, and Zayyan ibn Mardanish took control' (key dates 'independent from the Almohads 1228/9'). The year is the earlier of the page's two.

region.text: Puig and the country around Valencia

ledger.note: 1236: Aragon takes Puig. 'Aragon occupied nearby Puig, and Zayyan was defeated at the Battle of the Puig.'

region.text: Puig and the country around Valencia

ledger.note: 29 September 1238: the fighting ends with the surrender of Valencia. 'The city surrendered' after the siege that began 23 April 1238; Zayyan's request for Hafsid help failed when Catalan ships blocked the fleet.

29 September 1238: Valencia surrenders to James I. 'The city surrendered' (the Crown of Aragon dossier has 28 September; the Kingdom of Valencia page has James I entering the city on 9 October 1238, 'the dawn of the Kingdom of Valencia'). Zayyan escaped and ruled Murcia 1239-1241.

wars.name: Valencian occupation of Almería
wars.outcome: After Zuhayr's death the emir Abd al-Aziz of Valencia occupied Almería; it was independent again under Ma'n from 1041.
wars.note: Infobox 'To Valencia: 1038-1042'; the Murcian lands passed to Valencia in 1038 and stayed until 1065 (Murcia page).

wars.name: Toledan annexation of Valencia
wars.outcome: Al-Ma'mun of Toledo seized Valencia in 1065 and installed his vizier as governor.
wars.note: Ferdinand I attacked the city 'shortly after Abd al-Malik's accession' without taking it.

wars.name: El Cid's conquest of Valencia
wars.outcome: El Cid re-entered Valencia on 15 June 1094 after a 20-month siege that followed the coup of Ibn Jahhaf (October 1092); Ibn Jahhaf was later burned alive.
wars.note: The page's infobox says 1094, the text runs the siege from 1092 to 1094.

wars.name: Almoravid campaigns against Valencia
wars.outcome: The Almoravid relief army of September 1093 retreated; they besieged Valencia in October 1094 and were beaten; a 30,000-strong army besieged Peña Cadiella in late 1096; Mazdali besieged Valencia in early spring 1102 and the Almoravids occupied it in April-May 1102.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Valencia

zones.text: Puig and the country around Valencia

wars.outcome: Aragon took Puig in 1236, besieged Valencia from 23 April 1238, and the city surrendered on 29 September 1238.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Valencia page dates the conquest of the future kingdom from 1232 (Morella) and 1233 (Borriana, Peñíscola); those places lie north of Cliopatria's 1236 shape and no page opened names their holder.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given for the taifa's frontiers in any page opened; the extent of its district around Valencia is approximate throughout. The Treaty of Almizra (1244, after the taifa) is the first sharp line in the region.

notes:
IDENTITY. One state with long gaps: independent 1010-1065 (with Almería and Murcia 1038-1041/1065), Toledan 1065-1085, Castilian vassal then El Cid's 1085-1102, Almoravid 1102-1145, independent 1145-1147, inside Ibn Mardanish's Murcian realm 1147-1172 and Almohad 1172-1228, independent again 1228-1238, Aragonese from 29 September 1238. Cliopatria keeps shapes to 1249. The infobox area is not stated, so no area comparison was possible.
CLIOPATRIA CORRECTIONS. 1040 shape drawn from 1038 (Almería page); 1147 shape (53,704 km2, reaching Lleida) unsupported by the Valencia and Ibn Mardanish pages and replaced by the city shape for 1147; 1241 shape is no taifa (the state ends in 1238). New keyframes for 1041-1045, 1099-1102, 1145-1147 and 1228-1235 fill Cliopatria's gaps with its own shapes.
UNSETTLED. (1) Castile's dossier has no vassal_start for al-Qadir's Valencia (1086-1092, counterpart taifa-of-valencia); it should carry one and close it in October 1092. (2) The county of Barcelona's suzerainty over Labib (1017/18) and Mujahid of Dénia's hold over Valencia 1017-1021 (the Dénia dossier has the occupation) are not territorial in Cliopatria and are not in this ledger. (3) Which of Ibn Mardanish's lands (Jaén, Albarracín, Teruel, the Castellón coast) were governed from Valencia is not on the pages opened; the Murcia dossier owns the realm 1147-1172. (4) The Almohad takeover of Valencia in 1172 belongs to the Murcia dossier (Valencia was Murcian then). (5) The 28/29 September 1238 discrepancy between the Crown of Aragon and Valencia pages. (6) Who held Morella, Borriana and Peñíscola before 1232-1233 is not on any page opened. (7) The Murcia page's infobox gives Murcia to Valencia in 1145-1147 while its text lists 1145 independence; Valencia's own page has Ibn 'Iyad commanding Valencia and Murcia in 1146.
PAGES. Taifa of Valencia, Taifa of Almería, Taifa of Murcia, Muhammad ibn Sa'd ibn Mardanish, Kingdom of Valencia (five; the page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibn_Mardanish is only a disambiguation page and was not used). Taifa of Toledo, Ferdinand I and Alfonso VI were read for the Toledo dossier and not cited here.
GAZETTEER. Almenara and Puig (de Santa Maria) are not in places.jsonl; coordinate radii are used.
